title: WAN
notes: None — an extender has no internet connection of its own. It reaches the internet through the gateway, over its mesh backhaul link.

title: LAN
notes: An Ethernet port lets the extender use a wired backhaul link to the gateway instead of Wi-Fi, when one is available.

title: Wi-Fi
notes: Wi-Fi access point for wireless devices, covering 2.4, 5, and 6 GHz bands. Also used for the wireless mesh backhaul link back to the gateway.

title: EasyMesh
notes: This is what makes the device an extender — it joins a gateway's mesh as an agent, extending its Wi-Fi coverage.

title: Bluetooth / IoT

detail.label: Tested with
detail.value: TP-Link Tapo smart plug (Matter over Wi-Fi), onvis smart plug (Matter over Thread)

notes: Same multiprotocol radio as the gateway, for connecting smart-home devices if IoT support is enabled on the extender.

title: Voice
notes: Not applicable — an extender has no internet connection of its own, so it can't host SIP calling.

title: Packet Processor
notes: Not applicable — an extender doesn't route or NAT traffic, so there's nothing for this to accelerate.

title: AI / NPU
notes: Not present on this hardware today. A future board revision could add one as a plug-in module, for on-device AI features.

title: USB
notes: A general-purpose USB port, available for connecting IoT devices during testing.

title: Storage
notes: Onboard flash storage for the firmware, with A/B partitions so updates can be applied safely. An SD card slot is also available.

title: Media Tuner
notes: No tuner hardware — an extender has no WAN or voice functions.

title: Diagnostics
notes: A serial port for debugging during development. A local web page usually isn't needed on an extender.
